1. Core Clinical Tension: A 66-year-old woman presents with an isolated, painful calf mass, restricted knee motion, and bilateral lower-extremity sensory neuropathy mimicking a soft-tissue sarcoma, peripheral nerve sheath tumor, or autoimmune myopathy. Paradoxically, she lacked constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and tested negative on all routine systemic and tuberculosis-specific screening assays (PPD skin test, interferon-gamma release assay, sputum AFB smears, ESR, and normal tumor markers).
2. Admission Breakpoint: The point of admission evaluation and non-invasive multimodal imaging (chest CT, calf ultrasound, lower-extremity MRI, FDG-PET/CT, and electromyography), immediately preceding surgical open gastrocnemius muscle biopsy and frozen section tissue PCR.
3. Differential Distinctions: Soft-tissue sarcomas exhibit high proliferation indices and malignant cytology on biopsy; rheumatologic myopathies demonstrate abnormal autoantibodies (ANA, ANCA) and elevated ESR/muscle enzymes; muscular tuberculosis is characterized by deep necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with caseous necrosis, confirmed by targeted tissue molecular amplification even when systemic tuberculin tests are completely non-reactive.
case_prompt:
A 66-year-old woman presented for evaluation of a 1-month history of a painful isolated mass on the medial aspect of the left calf, accompanied by bilateral numbness in her toes. She reported household contact with relatives who had suffered from chronic pulmonary and pleural illnesses years earlier (her father 10 years prior and her daughter 7 years prior). She remained in good general condition and denied systemic constitutional symptoms, including night sweats, weight loss, anorexia, fatigue, or intermittent fevers.

On physical examination, she had a tender mass with irregular, indistinct borders palpated in the left calf. Active and passive left lower-extremity mobility was severely restricted by knee pain. Neurological examination showed a mild decrease in distal sensation and mild swelling of the lower extremities. The overlying skin was normal without erythema, warmth, or trophic breakdown. No mass was palpable in the contralateral right leg.

Routine laboratory evaluation revealed normal complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), procalcitonin, liver and renal function tests, antinuclear antibodies (ANA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), fungal (1,3)-beta-D-glucan test, and serum tumor markers. Serological testing showed a mildly elevated rheumatoid factor of 33.8 IU/mL (reference range: up to 15 IU/mL), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein of 7.48 mg/L (reference range: up to 3 mg/L), and positive antistreptolysin O (ASO). Electromyography demonstrated reduced motor and sensory nerve conduction velocities in the lower limbs, decreased compound motor action potentials, and decreased sensory nerve action potential amplitudes, indicative of extensive chronic neurogenic lesions.

Chest computed tomography showed scattered bilateral inflammatory changes in the inferior pulmonary lobes with bilateral nodular pleural thickening. Bilateral calf ultrasonography revealed a 50 x 16-mm hypoechoic mass in the left soleus muscle and a 43 x 6-mm hypoechoic lesion in the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle. Whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated multiple hypermetabolic muscular lesions in the bilateral lower extremities, with the largest lesion in the left soleus muscle measuring 33.8 x 20 x 42 mm and demonstrating an SUVmax of 15.9. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the calves demonstrated hyperintense, gadolinium-enhancing intramuscular masses in the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles bilaterally.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Strongly suspected due to an intensely hypermetabolic, deeply infiltrative intramuscular mass (SUVmax 15.9) in an older adult; however, biopsy revealed epithelioid granulomas with caseous necrosis without cytokeratin immunoreactivity and a very low Ki-67 proliferative index (10%).
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Microscopic examination for acid-fast bacilli stain and cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) was completely negative. CD3, CD31, CD34, desmin, Kp1, and PGM1 staining were weakly positive. The Ki67 labeling index was low (10%).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because of positive rheumatoid factor, elevated high-sensitivity CRP, positive ASO, and peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; but ESR, antinuclear antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were normal, and muscle histopathology did not show inflammatory vasculitis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Further clinical examinations, including hemogram, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), procalcitonin test (PCT), liver and renal function tests, antinuclear antibody (ANA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), fungal G-test, and tumor marker levels, returned results within normal limits.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The definitive diagnosis was established by left gastrocnemius muscle biopsy demonstrating nodular epithelioid granulomas with central caseous necrosis, corroborated by positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex PCR specifically on frozen muscle sections, despite negative sputum, blood, urine, PPD, and IGRA testing.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: PCR for the mycobacterium tuberculosis complex in blood, urine, sputum, and paraffin-embedded samples from case 1 returned negative results; however, the result was positive in frozen sections of muscles.

editor_comments: Zero spoilers in case prompt; strictly excluded PPD, IGRA, AFB, and muscle biopsy from presentation narrative. Verbatim quotes validated.
